observations: A roughly four-by-four grid of rounded rectangular shapes fills the canvas, each containing a simplified face with looping eyes, noses, and mouths drawn in heavy black lines.
A saturated purple-violet field dominates the background, interrupted by streaks of orange, yellow, white, and pink that cross over and between the face compartments.
Faces vary in fill color—muted green, peach, lavender, gray—giving each cell a distinct tonal identity despite the uniform black outlines binding them together.
reading: The grid reads like a crowd pressed together, each face boxed in yet bleeding into its neighbors through tangled overlapping lines. Some mouths gape with visible teeth; others flatten into thin curves. The purple ground pushes the warmer fills forward, creating a sense of faces surfacing from noise. The effect can feel claustrophobic or communal depending on where the eye rests—every cell competes for attention, none fully wins.
contextAngle: In the owned Scrimshaw subset, this work sits between Scrimshaw9 and Scrimshaw13 by title number. Where Scrimshaw9 isolates a single head against open peach space, Scrimshaw12 multiplies faces into a packed field, shifting from solitary figure to dense crowd.

connections.reason: Scrimshaw13 shares heavy black outlines and looping spiral eyes but returns to a single large face, making the grid compression here a distinct structural choice.
nnxyz nifty faces #11 builds a face from dense tangled lines across the whole canvas; Scrimshaw12 distributes that same density across many smaller compartments.

lookingQuestion: Do the faces along the edges—partially cropped by the border—seem to extend the crowd beyond the visible frame, or does the grid feel like a closed, contained set?
ambiguities: The exact count of distinct faces is hard to fix; overlapping lines merge some cells, making it unclear whether certain compartments hold one face or two.
Some colored streaks (orange, white) may be separate drawing layers or part of the face outlines—their role is visually ambiguous.
